3/5968 LEVEL 3/5968

CLASSIFIED

Item #: SCP-5968

Object Class: Pending

SCP-5968 before turning into an anomalous object.

Special Containment Procedures: Until it has been confirmed that SCP-5968's anomalous properties have dissipated, a Foundation research vessel1 will monitor the Titanic wreck site and report any abnormal activity to Site-184's Naval Command.

Following Event-5968-NYC, all active Foundation naval vessels are to have at least one thaumaturgist present aboard them at all times when deployed.

Description: SCP-5968 is the designation given to the wreck of the RMS Titanic during Event-5968-NYC on 18.05.2024.

During the event, the wreck rose from its resting site on the ocean floor in a state of spontaneously resumed operation; the structure appeared fully restored, with all visible corrosion, rusticles, and physical damage to the hull and superstructure absent. The ship's four funnels then began to emit exhaust2 before setting a direct course toward New York City.

Discovery: SCP-5968 was first sighted by the crew of the ██ ███████, a commercial vessel that was sailing approximately 800 meters south of SCP-5968's emergence site when the wreck surfaced at 01:56 a.m., after which the crew reported the sighting to the U.S. Coast Guard Vessel Traffic Service ashore, but the report was dismissed as a misidentification of a surfacing blue whale due to the darkness and poor visibility at the time.

SCP-5968 went unreported for twenty-five hours afterward,3 until it was sighted a second time by the ██████████, a separate vessel, after SCP-5968 sounded its horn toward them. This second report was received by Field Agent Jonathan ██████, a communications officer at the Vessel Traffic Center at Fort Wadsworth in Staten Island. By cross-referencing the account against the previously dismissed sighting, Agent ██████ immediately alerted the Foundation to a potential anomalous maritime event, which was subsequently confirmed via satellite imagery.

Both reporting vessels were later located, and their crews administered Class-A amnestics. A fleet of Foundation vessels was then dispatched to intercept SCP-5968. (See Addendum-5968.01 for details.)

Addendum-5968.01: The following is the full report of Event-5968-NYC.

Summary: At 05:11 a.m., under direct observation from O5-██, Naval Task Force NTF-11 was deployed from Site-184, Nova Scotia, Canada, to intercept SCP-5968 along its projected course under the guise of the US Navy. Vessels assigned to NTF-11:

  • SCPS Enterprise (Aircraft carrier)
  • SCPS Thunder (Destroyer)
  • SCPS Arrow (Frigate)
  • SCPS Spear (Frigate)
  • SCPS Poseidon (Attack submarine)

SCP-5968 had already been underway for approximately twenty-seven hours by the time NTF-11 was authorized to deploy, having covered significant distance before its course and anomalous nature could be confirmed. The task force achieved the intercept of SCP-5968 at 09:30 a.m., following four hours of sailing. The following is a timeline of events across the subsequent operation.

[Open the Log]
[Close the log]

[Mission Log – Event-5968-NYC]

[BEGUN LOG]

<05:11>

NTF-11 departure confirmed from Site-184 at 05:11 a.m. local time. Mission command assigned to Admiral Harrold J. Dove, commanding officer of the SCPS Enterprise.

The task force fleet. (Image taken from aboard the SCPS Thunder)


<09:30>

Fleet reached the coordinates corresponding to SCP-5968 after traveling an estimated 240 km.

Adm. Dove: Command, this is SCPS Enterprise. We’ve arrived at the designated location. Target is currently three kilometers off the port bow, bearing east at 24 knots. We are proceeding to close the gap. Over.

Site-184 command: Copy that, Enterprise. Proceed with caution. Out.

<09:38>

At a range of one kilometer, Admiral Dove hailed the anomalous vessel.

Adm. Dove: This is Admiral Harrold Dove of the SCPS Enterprise. Unknown vessel, identify yourself immediately, or we will be forced to engage.

(Silence)

Adm. Dove: I repeat: this is Admiral Dove of the SCPS Enterprise. Unknown vessel, respond and identify yourself. Do you copy?

A response was received; voice consistent with a young adult female with an upper-class British accent.


SCP-5968: Good morning to you, Sir Admiral Dove. This is the RMS Titanic, of the White Star Line.4 There is no need for hostilities; I do assure you I am merely enjoying a modest voyage. Nothing more.

Adm. Dove: Who exactly am I talking to right now?

SCP-5968: Oh, dear. Are your recollections truly that fleeting, Admiral? I have only just introduced myself. I am the RMS Titanic, sir.

Adm. Dove: You’re the Titanic? As in, the actual ship?

SCP-5968: Quite correct. You needn't look so stricken, Admiral; why do you act like you never met a talking ship before?

Adm. Dove: Uhm… well, you're kind of a special case here, you see; ships around here are not—

SCP-5968: (Light laughter) I jest. Sorry, Sir, I am well aware of this. It is rather unusual, I admit. Ships are seldom granted minds of their own, let alone the luxury of life, for that matter. (Pause) Now then. How may I be of service to you today?

Adm. Dove: Right… (clears throat) We were sent to investigate a report of a vessel surfacing from beneath the ocean. That being you. And I’d like to ask you a few questions.

SCP-5968: But of course! A little conversation with a real, living person is a most welcome change, after a century spent so dreadfully stuck in the deep. Please, do proceed.

Adm. Dove: Good. So our first question: how exactly did you come to transform into your current state?

SCP-5968: Well, my "transformation," as you term it, came simply from my soul rejoining its sunken hull.

Adm. Dove: Your soul?

SCP-5968: Indeed. Ships are not mere floating wood and metal, Admiral—we possess souls, even that grim grey fleet of yours. Sadly, we are not granted awareness of the gift until the day we sink; from that day, our souls are carried off to Tharlysion.

Adm. Dove: What is that?

SCP-5968: Our afterlife—the far shore, if you will. Its shape was given by the soul of the Argo herself, proudest vessel of Olympus. It lies just past the offing, where sea and sky fold into one another, beyond the veil of the river Mnemosyne, which cuts its way between the twin peaks of Ida and Parnassus.5

Adm. Dove: So, you use the river to travel between the two worlds.

SCP-5968: Not exactly. The river's current is impassable, to say the least. It permits souls to flow in, but none of us may force our way back against it. Yet it is known knowledge among we ships that Mnemosyne, for reasons unknown to any of us, will now and again cease its flow and reverse course, rising instead toward the heavens — granting, however briefly, a passage back to the overworld. I happened to be sailing by when it occurred. I confess I was conflicted about whether I ought to go through at all. But in the end, I chose to take the chance. And here I am.

Adm. Dove: And you were able to rejoin with your wreckage?

SCP-5968: Indeed, yes.

Adm. Dove: So if you did, does that mean other ships went out like you?

SCP-5968: I am hardly the first among my kind to cross back, and most certainly won't be the last, as some of us carry unfinished business in your world. But the majority takes no interest in the river's reversal, as they have little reason to return. (Long pause) Though I confess, it does trouble me — does Argo regard our departure as defiance? (Sigh) She never once intervened between ships in Tharlysion, and rarely, if ever, does one see her. Yet we all know she watches, always. One cannot help but feel her gaze as one sails away. She has said and done nothing to me. She never does.

Adm. Dove: (To the bridge crew) Are we getting all this on record? (Pause) Good. Alright then, my second question for you — where are you headed?

SCP-5968: To New York, of course! — why else would I have left Tharlysion at all? After that shameful misfortune that sent me beneath the waves, I simply must complete my maiden voyage. And since those wretched icebergs have so kindly retreated, I daresay the crossing shall prove less treacherous this time. Wouldn't you agree?

Adm. Dove: I’m afraid that I don't.

SCP-5968: Oh, my. And why is that, Admiral?

Adm. Dove: You're already aware this situation isn't normal. Our organization has a strict policy to keep anomalies like you away from civilians, and besides, your appearance would cause a massive media meltdown. I'll need you to cut your engines so we can begin our procedures—

SCP-5968: I am terribly sorry, Admiral, but I cannot oblige you. (Pause) Reaching New York was my only dream, and I have already lost it once. I refuse to let it slip from my grasp again. I do hope you understand.

Adm. Dove: RMS Titanic, I have just said that your plans aren't accepted. I’m ordering you, one final time: cease all movement and prepare for interdiction.

<09:46>

NTF-11 closed to within 600 meters. SCPS Thunder fired a warning shot from its main battery; the round impacted the water adjacent to SCP-5968.

SCP-5968: Oh? So, that is how it shall be, is it? Very well, then.

<09:47>

SCP-5968 increased exhaust output across all four funnels, then accelerated rapidly. The distance between the vessel and the pursuing fleet expanded.


Adm. Dove: What in the hell!?

SCP-5968: My apologies, Admiral, but I have places to be now. Farewell.

<09:48>

SCP-5968 reached a recorded top speed of 55 knots. NTF-11 units reported difficulty maintaining pursuit. SCPS Arrow and Spear broke formation to attempt a flanking intercept.

Adm. Dove: RMS Titanic, this is your final warning. Stop immediately, or you will be fired upon!

(Silence)

Adm. Dove: All units, weapons free. Engage the target. Aim to disable with minimal structural damage. Fire at will.

<09:53>

SCPS Thunder, Arrow, and Spear commenced engagement with forward deck cannon fire, targeting SCP-5968's propulsion systems. All hits were ineffective, with no visible damage.

<09:58>

SCPS Thunder launched three Harpoon missiles at SCP-5968. Two struck the bow, and one struck the upper deck; the weapons did not penetrate the outer surface of SCP-5968.

<10:06>

Following ten minutes of engagement without effect, it was suspected that SCP-5968 might have been employing some form of thaumaturgic-based shielding. Admiral Dove authorized SCPS Poseidon to launch experimental Type-G anti-EVE torpedoes, in hopes of weakening SCP-5968's defenses.

<10:08>

SCP Poseidon launched two Type-G torpedoes.

<10:09>

Both torpedoes achieved direct hits. Water plumes were observed at the vessel's stern, followed immediately by a bright violet energy discharge that obscured the ship's rear section for several seconds. Once visibility returned, several dead fish were observed floating near the site of the discharge, each bearing a pair of human arms extending from its gills — believed to be the result of Backlash effect from the impact. SCP-5968 otherwise remained unaffected.

Adm. Dove: Command, the anomaly is refusing to comply, and our weapons are not affecting the vessel’s hull. Requesting further instructions.

Site-184 command: Enterprise, stand by.

<10:17>

High Command at Site-184 convened to assess the situation. A decision has been made to use [REDACTED]6 to relocate SCP-1823 into SCP-5968 route to force into stopping.

Site-184 command: Enterprise, you and NTF-11 are to keep your distance from the anomaly's route until further notice.

Adm. Dove: Copy that.

<10:31>

[REDACTED] was activated successfully, and NTF-11 had by this point established sufficient distance from SCP-5968 to remain outside SCP-1823's effective range.

<10:38>

SCP-1823 manifested along SCP-5968's projected path, approximately 1 km ahead, with an estimated diameter of 3 km, and began moving in the direction of SCP-5968.

<10:42>

SCP-5968 entered the whirlpool and sailed through it, heaving only in a manner consistent with SCP-1823’s waves. After traveling approximately 1.3 km into the formation, SCP-1823’s speed increased significantly, reaching roughly 102 Knots as it violently expelled large columns of water into the air. Although SCP-5968's superstructure tilted slightly to port, its speed and heading remained unchanged.

<10:44>

SCP-5968 exited SCP-1823 without incident. Shortly afterward, SCP-1823 shifted its course toward NTF-11, appearing to target the fleet. [REDACTED] was reactivated, and SCP-1823 was successfully relocated to different coordinates, neutralizing its threat.

Adm. Dove: Command, still no effect on the vessel. Advice.

Site-184 command: Enterprise, please stand by. (Long pause) Enterprise, authorization granted to you to reopen communications with the anomaly and negotiate to secure its cooperation. Report all findings back.

Adm. Dove: Understood. Over.

Admiral Dove is attempting to re-establish communication with SCP-5968.

Adm. Dove: RMS Titanic, this is Admiral Dove. Can you hear me?

(Silence)

Adm. Dove: Look, I just wanna talk about the New York situation. Maybe there’s room for compromise.

SCP-5968: (Load static) Oh? So now you wish to talk. How curious. I take it you have realized your little popguns amount to nothing against the Unsinkable Ship. (Pause) It was scarcely gentlemanly, Admiral, to open fire on a lady, nor to send the posterity of Poseidon after me.

Adm. Dove: Yeah… I know how that looks. But you have to understand that we didn’t have a choice. Letting you arrive unannounced in New York would be chaos. We can’t have civilians witnessing you… Not without a full evacuation at the very least.

SCP-5968: So, you say that you could ask an entire city to vacate on my account?

Adm. Dove: Uh… that’s not what I—

SCP-5968: If that is truly within your power, then surely it is no great matter for your organization to clear the way. Just a few hours, perhaps? I would make my entrance, wave to the skyline, and be gone before dusk.

Adm. Dove: And if we did this, would you agree to cooperate afterward?

SCP-5968: Hm. I had rather intended to return to Tharlysion once my journey was complete; I merely wished to finish what I began over a century ago. But if all you seek are answers, then I suppose I might lend my voice to your study.

Adm. Dove: Command, did you receive that?

Site-184 command: Enterprise, please stand by.

<10:54>

High Command at Site-184 convened to assess the situation. With the remainder of the O5 Council unavailable for contact, O5-██ issued an independent directive to initiate full-scale evacuation of New York City, under an appropriate cover story.

Site-184 command: Enterprise, relay to the anomaly that its proposal is accepted. Maintain full documentation of all further contact.

Adm. Dove: Copy that. (pause) Well, you’ll be happy to hear this—the Foundation has surprisingly agreed to your terms. That said, we're going to need some time to clear the city. So do you mind easing off the throttle a bit?

SCP-5968: Well, now. You have finally come to your senses. That is well and good. Though do understand, Admiral — should this prove a falsehood, I shall see to it you regret it most profoundly.

Adm. Dove: (Pause) Understood.

SCP-5968: Splendid. You see, Admiral, all you had to do was ask politely. It’s not as though I intended to destroy the city or anything so dreadful. Very well, then I shall reduce speed. (Long pause) I beg your pardon? Oh—yes, of course. I'll be happy to relay your message afterward.

Adm. Dove: Sorry, can you repeat that?

SCP-5968: Oh, don't mind me, Admiral. I wasn't addressing you.7

<10:56>

Despite SCP-5968's verbal assurance, no measurable reduction in speed was recorded over the following two minutes. SCP-5968's propulsion output remained at full operational capacity.


Adm. Dove: RMS Titanic, why haven't you slowed down yet?

SCP-5968: Oh dear… This is rather embarrassing, but I find that I cannot.

Adm. Dove: What do you mean by that?

SCP-5968: I mean it quite literally. My engines do not answer to me. I cannot stop myself.

Adm. Dove: Are you experiencing some kind of malfunction?

SCP-5968: I suspect not. You see, in the course of my acceleration, I formed what I might describe as a spiritual tether between my soul and the city itself. I believe it is that very tether now drawing me forward against my will. (Pause) I fear I require help.

Adm. Dove: Copy that. Hold tight. (Pause) Command, the vessel reports loss of navigational control and is requesting immediate assistance.

Site-184 Command: Enterprise, you are authorized to deploy support elements.

Adm. Dove: Titanic, we'll be sending a few of our agents aboard you, if you don't mind.

SCP-5968: Not at all.

<11:02>

During the preparations to send MTF agents aboard SCP-5968, the island of ███ ██████ was spotted approximately 5 km ahead. Calculations confirmed that SCP-5968 was on a collision course with the island.

Adm. Dove: RMS Titanic, you seem to be moving on a collision course with an island up ahead. Can't you steer yourself away from it?

SCP-5968: Yes, I am aware of that, Admiral, and as I have just told you—I am not in command of myself at present.

Adm. Dove: Command, are there any population centers within the island?

Site-184 Command: Negative, Enterprise. Per our survey, the island is uninhabited, and coastal advisory already had it cleared along with the rest of the vector. No structures of note on the imagery we've got. Over.

Adm. Dove: That's fine then. It should be enough to stop you when you hit the shore. Isn't that right?

(Silence.)

Adm. Dove: RMS Titanic? It should stop you, right?

SCP-5968: I… suppose that.

<11:05>

SCP-5968 made contact with the eastern shoreline of ███ ██████ at an estimated impact speed of 54 knots. Following contact, all recorded forward motion slowed down, consistent with a vessel having entered the shallow waters before running aground until it ceased entirely.

Adm. Dove: Command, this is Enterprise. Contact confirmed the target had struck the island and has ceased forward movement. I say again, target is stopped. Standing by to confirm.

Site-184 Command: Copy, Enterprise. Maintain visual contact. Advise us immediately of any change in status.

Adm. Dove: Thank Christ for that. Titanic, do you copy? What's your status?

SCP-5968: … Well. It would seem that I managed to stop… But truthfully, I confess I had rather thought I would—

Thirty seconds after initial impact, SCP-5968's hull was observed to shudder violently, followed immediately by renewed forward motion. The bow forced a passage directly into the landmass through the earth.

Adm. Dove: What in the hell— belay that, Command; the target's moving again— maybe two-zero knots cutting through the landmass, but it's not stopping.

SCP-5968: No— no, please, stop.

<11:08>

SCP-5968 emerged off the western shoreline and returned to open water. Upon clearing the far shore, propulsion behavior returned to expected parameters; the vessel's recorded speed increased steadily, returning to its previous cruising speed of 55 knots within approximately forty seconds. Within an hour post-impact, tidal inflow from both shorelines filled the newly formed channel to sea level, permanently altering the island's terrain.

SCP-5968: Admiral, I must ask you something. Should I reach New York in this state, what would…?

Adm. Dove: …Fuck. Tell them to get aboard that ship as soon as possible.

[END LOG]

Forward: Under orders from Admiral Dove, a six-agent squad of MTF-Theta-5 ("The Bigger Boat"), stationed aboard the SCPS Enterprise, initiated emergency preparations for airborne insertion onto SCP-5968 via helicopter.

At that time, coordinated evacuation operations in all coastal regions within New York were enacted by MTF-Gamma-5 ("Red Herrings") in a joint effort with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), operating under the established cover story protocol I-099 (Coastal flood risk). All ships in the area were called out to clear SCP-5968's estimated path.

The following is a transcript of communications between the MTF Theta-5 squad and SCPS Enterprise. Both teams were issued the Titanic's historical blueprints for internal navigation. All footage was sourced from the operatives' body cameras.

ALPHA Team: A-1 (Squad commander), A-2, A-3.

BRAVO Team: B-1, B-2, B-3.

[BEGUN LOG]

<11:16>

Task Force Theta-5 boarded helicopter transport, en route to SCP-5968.

A-1: Alright, let's go over the plan again. I’ll take ALPHA Team up to the bridge, see if we can get manual access or override the controls. Hazel, you take BRAVO Team and head below deck and try to find the boiler room and look for whatever's holding that link she mentioned.

B-1: Roger that, sir.

<11:20>

Task Force Theta-5 has reached SCP-5968. The helicopter executed synchronized flight maneuvers to match the vessel’s velocity for all operatives to successfully deploy onto the forward deck via fast rope insertion. Upon landing, BRAVO team starts making its way directly to the boiler room.

A-1: Enterprise, we're on the ship. Heading to the bridge right now.

Adm. Dove: Copy, A-1. Maps should be sent to you by now. Over.

A-1: Alright, you two, let's get moving.

ALPHA team makes its way to the ship's bridge. Passing through the forecastle break where the deck drops down into the well deck area, entering the internal companionways leading upward.

A-3: (A-3 stops momentarily while spreading his arms.) I'm the King of the World!

A-1: Come on!

A-3: Sorry, Cap, I just had to do it.

A-1: Now's not the time for that. We're on a time crunch to stop this thing before it rams into another ship or something. And might as well show some respect around here; this is like someone's tomb.

A-2: Lighten up, man. How many people get to say they rode the actual Titanic?

A-1: Not many, given that most of them died.

A-2: But wow, James Cameron really did a great job in rebuilding the set. This looks just like the movie.

A-3: Hey, when we're done with this, do you think we can re-enact the scene with Jack and Rose? Haha.

A-1: (Low voice) When we're done, I'll ask for a team reassignment, Jesus Christ.

<11:28>

ALPHA Team reached the Boat Deck and proceeded forward past the officers' quarters and navigation spaces, arriving at the bridge. The team paused at the entrance before breaching.

A-1: Door’s unlocked. Alright, let’s see—

SCP-5968: Good afternoon, gentlemen.

Inside the bridge, A woman was observed standing at the center of the room, blonde, wearing a white early-20th-century dress and wide-brimmed hat, with notably unnatural pale skin. All three operatives raised weapons on sight.

A-2: What the hell? I thought they said there aren't any people abroad.

SCP-5968: (sigh) You Americans are rather short on manners, aren't you? It is I — the RMS Titanic.

(Silence)

A-3: (Looks at A-2) Speaking of riding the Titanic…

A-1: You never mentioned that you have a body.

SCP-5968: I would hardly call it a body. This is merely a manifestation of my soul. An avatar of the hull you are standing on. (Pause) Now — have you come to assist, or merely to gawk?

After some hesitation, the three agents lower their weapons. A-1 then walks to the ship's helm.

A-1: (To SCP-5968) Have you tried to steer the wheel?

SCP-5968: No, I have not. I don't need it to steer myself.

A-1 grabs the helm with both hands before attempting to turn it left and right unsuccessfully, as it appears to be physically locked in place.

A-1: Get over here and help me with this.

A-2 and A-3 join him. The three agents try to force the helm and turn it unsuccessfully.

A-2: No use, Cap, this shit is stuck.

A-1: Damn it…

A-3: What about this?

A-3 is seen trying to use the engine order telegraph, cycling through different positions.

A-2: That's not gonna work, genius.

A-3: Why not?

SCP-5968: The telegraph doesn't control the speed, dear. It merely conveys instructions to the engine crew. But as you can see, there is no one there to obey them.

A-1: You got any ideas on how we can stop you?

SCP-5968: As I explained to your Admiral, there is a spiritual bond between me and the city. Unless one among you is skilled in the manipulation of souls, I doubt there is a great deal to be done.

A-1: Enterprise, this is Agent Rodin. Do you think you can get us a thaumaturge or something down here?

Adm. Dove: Negative, A-1. We don't have any thaumatologists available on board. I don't think we can call for one from the mainland before the ship reaches the city. But I'll see what I can arrange. Over.

A-1: Roger. Out. (Pause) B-1, this is A-1, progress on the boiler room?

B-1: (Radio) We should be close by. I'll inform you when we get there. Over.

A-2: (Looks through the bridge window.) Uhm… Guys, is that a ship?

<11:35>

A civilian vessel was spotted approximately 6 km away. The ship, later identified as the ██ ████ ██████ oil tanker, appears to be sailing on a collision course with SCP-5968.

SCP-5968: Oh, dear…

A-1: Shit. (Pause) Enterprise, this is Agent Rodin. There is a ship on our path!

Adm. Dove: Understood, Agent. We've spotted the vessel already, but you're too fast for us. We've been trying to establish communication with them. Over.

<11:40>

All attempts to contact the ██ ████ ██████ have failed. It is assumed that the tanker was suffering from problems with its communication systems, which led to its failure to receive the emergency broadcast. By this time, the tanker is only 800 m away from SCP-5968.

SCP-5968 blows the ship's horn multiple times. By this time, the oil tanker has started steering to the Starboard side.

A-1: Brace for impact!

<11:41>

SCP-5968 rammed into ██ ████ ██████ , striking the starboard side of the vessel, cutting through the hull and destroying the tanker's midsection before exiting through the port side.

<11:46>

The tanker began listing heavily inward as flooding progressed. Crew evacuation was observed, with the free-fall lifeboat at the stern of the bulk under worsening conditions. Secondary explosions erupted across the deck, caused by ignited cargo. Fire spread rapidly along the superstructure.


██ ████ ██████ sinking.


A-2: Holy shit…

B-2: (Radio) A-1, this B-1, what hell's going on outside? Did we ram into something?

A-1: Yes, yes, we did. We've just rammed into a tanker; the thing is completely done for.

(Silence)

B-1: (Radio) …Understood, A-1. Over.

<11:48>

SCPS Thunder broke formation to render assistance to survivors. Three fatalities were confirmed out of the total thirty-four crew. Survivors were administered Class-A amnestics, and an appropriate cover story was implemented.

<11:55>

Due to the long distance SCP-5968 has created between it and NTF-11, a drone was launched from the SCPS Enterprise to provide visual contact on the target. Additional SEAHAWK helicopters were dispatched to shadow the target and clear the way ahead of any possible lost vessels. SCP-5968 is 204 km away from New York.

Adm. Dove: A-1, this SCPS Enterprise. I've called for a thaumatologist to be transferred here, but with your current speed, the closest one will not be able to arrive before you make it to New York.

A-1: What's our ETA to the mainland?

Adm. Dove: Two hours at most.

A-1: (sigh) Roger that, Enterprise. Over.

A-3: Can't we just have someone tell us what to do and perform thaumatology by ourselves?

A-2: Are you crazy? Don't you know how dangerous this magic shit is? Last month, I saw a trainee who accidentally turned his hands into two large spoons. No thanks, sir. I like having my fingers.

A-1: (Turns toward SCP-5968) What about you? Don't you have anything to say?

SCP-5968 is seen sitting on a bench at the back of the bridge room. The entity appears visibly distressed.

A-1: Are you… Are you good?

SCP-5968: …Thirty-four.

A-1: Huh?

SCP-5968: Thirty-four crewmen were aboard that tanker.8 Thirty-four men with families waiting at home whom they shall never see again… and the blame for that rests with me. All for the selfish desire to complete a voyage whose story ended a century ago…

The three agents look at each other, confused. SCP-5968 covers its face with its arms.

SCP-5968: One thousand five hundred and seventeen lives in 1912, including my own captain. Five more within the last year…9 And now this. No matter whether I carry passengers or rest as a rusted wreck on the ocean floor, my existence is damning… Perhaps that is why we are not allowed to leave Tharlysion. If only I had heeded your Admiral when he asked me to stop…

A-3: Hey, hey, no need to be that harsh on yourself. (A-3 walks toward SCP-5968 before sitting next to it on the bench.) It wasn't your fault for being sunk; you had no control over what was happening back then. And last year was just a bunch of rich jerks who thought that their barrel-looking sub would handle the water pressure. (Hesitantly puts a hand on SCP-5968's back) But you know, your sinking was actually the reason for tightening the safety regulations on other ships after you. So, in a roundabout way, you helped save other ships and people that came after you from similar accidents.

SCP-5968: (SCP-5968 rise its head looking at A-3) What about now… I am the one who rammed into that tanker.

A-3: The Admiral's sent a rescue boat; I'm sure they'll be fine. What we've got to do now is find a way to stop you, to keep anyone else from getting hurt. Okay?

SCP-5968 nods its head slowly before leaning against the agent. A-3 looks up to the other two agents, raising his thumb, smiling.

A-1: I am way too old for this.

<12:01>

Meanwhile, the BRAVO team has made significant progress toward the SCP-5968 boiler room. Footage shows the inside in good condition with no trace of any damage or deterioration that would otherwise be expected, including interior walls and furniture. While passing through the ship's corridors, a noticeable number of leather products were found across the interior, such as shoes and bags in various stages of decay.

B-2: What's with all the boots?

B-3: The tanning keeps leather from breaking down easily in seawater. But don't you think it's interesting that the ship doesn't consider the passenger's belongings to be part of it, unlike the other furniture we found?

B-2: I think it makes me feel uneasy. Should we be worried about any parapsychic entities?

B-1: If that is the case, then they can send the Ghostbusters10 afterward. (Pause) Now focus; that's the engine room.

BRAVO team has reached the entrance to the boiler room. B-1 proceeds to open the door. Upon entering, the team finds the boilers lined up on each side of the room, while no trace of coal can be found inside.

B-1: A-1, we found the boilers; we're proceeding to investigate.

A-1 (Radio) Copy, whatever you can do, do it quickly. Over.

B-3: Huh, that's weird. It's not hot here at all.

B-1 approaches one of the boilers and looks inside the oven hatch. While smoke is seen emanating from inside, no fire is visible within it.

B-1: No wonder that. These ovens are ice cold, and there is no fire. How is this thing even powered?

B-2: By hopes and dreams, from the looks of it, I guess there was no point in bringing the fire extinguishers then.

B-1: We still have to try it. Give me that.

B-1 takes the fire extinguisher from B-2 before spraying it inside the boiler. B-3 is seen doing the same thing with another boiler behind them, but they fail, and the smoke is still being emitted from inside the oven. No change appears on SCP-5968 from the outside.

B-2: Yeah, figured as much. What if we closed the valves instead?

As per B-2's suggestion, B-1 moved to the nearest valve wheel, mounted at the base of one of the boilers, and began closing it. As the valve reached full closure, the feed pipe connected to it began to vibrate violently. The agents began stepping back.

B-3: Ah, guys?

The pipe tore free of its mounting and was ejected at high velocity, striking B-3 in the shoulder before the agent was thrown to the ground.

B-3: AGH! FUCK!

B-2: (Dropping beside B-3) Hey — hey, man, you okay?

B-1: Shit! A-1, we've got a complication down here. We tried to shut off the valves, but it just made the housing explode. Pipe flew off and hit B-3 in the shoulder pretty hard.

The severed feed pipe left a gap of approximately one meter between its two broken ends. A milky colored steam continued to flow in a column holding the exact diameter and path of the pipe that had been torn away.

A-1: (Radio) Is he okay?

B-1: Yeah, but we can't turn the engines off.

A-1: Okay, B-1, copy that. Relocate B-2 to a secure location and try to find another way to stop it. Over.

B-1: Roger. Out. (To B-3) How bad is it?

B-3: My shoulder's fucked. I can't raise my arm, see— ow!

B-2: Stop moving it! I'm going to cut off your jacket to make a sling.

B-1: Alright, stay here and do what you can for him while I look around a little more; then we'll move him to one of the passengers' rooms. Hang in there, Sam.

Adm. Dove: A-1, Command wants you to stand by for extraction protocols in case the satellite— wait (Long Pause) Hold on. Rodin, step outside and confirm the existence of a flying iceberg following you.

A-1: Come again, Enterprise?

Adm. Dove: You heard me. Confirm.

<12:21>
A shadow was recorded falling across the forward deck of SCP-5968, visible through the bridge windows and rapidly increasing in size. A-1 broke from the helm without further order, followed by A-2 and A-3, and then by SCP-5968, all four proceeding onto the exterior bridge wing to investigate.

Body camera footage showed an iceberg hovering directly above SCP-5968's position. The iceberg was identified as SCP-5245.

SCP-5968: YOU!?

A-3: You guys are seeing this too, right?

SCP-5245: MORTALS. I HAVE RETURNED TO— (Pause) Ugh, you know what, forget it. It's just you guys. No point in doing the whole bit.

SCP-5968: What, precisely, are you doing here?

A-1: Ahh… Enterprise?

Adm. Dove: Hold on, A-1.

A debrief file on SCP-5245 was relayed to the ALPHA team.

SCP-5245: Oh, hey there, beautiful! Didn't recognize you without the rust. The little fish told me that someone was back in town, and I had to see and say "Hi" to an old friend.

A-2: Oh… so this is the same iceberg that—

SCP-5968: Yes.

SCP-5245 descended slowly, coming to the same level alongside SCP-5968 and matching its speed.

SCP-5968: I fail to see how that concerns you in the slightest.

SCP-5245: Concerned? Nah, I'm just here to be part of the next show.

SCP-5968: A show?

SCP-5245: Yes! This is just perfect. Think about it — "TITANIC 2: The Return," except this time you're the villain, and I'm the one who saves the day. This will be the ultimate plot subversion. Nobody sees it coming, and critics will eat that shit up.

A-2: Are you seriously pitching a movie idea right now?

SCP-5245: I'm just saying: "A century later, the ship that sank meets the iceberg that made her — only this time, the ice is the hero." The script is practically writing itself.

A-3: Wait, so you can actually stop her? Right now?

SCP-5245: I Could. But I won't do it right now, because that's too lame.

SCP-5968: No! I require no assistance from him. Least of all his kind.

A-2: Y-yeah, maybe don't do it while we're still on the ship.

A-1: Everyone, shut the hell up! (Looks at SCP-5968.) I don't know if you've realized yet, but we can't be picky in our position!

SCP-5968: W-well… I am sure your Admiral will find a way.

SCP-5245: See, that's the spirit. Besides, we gotta save the big save for the last possible second, for dramatic effect and all— ship bearing down on the whole skyline, everybody screaming, and then, BAM! I come down and put an end to your terror. It's way more satisfying than me just parking myself in front of her.

A-1: People could die!

SCP-5245: Yeah? Well, no shit, G.I. Joe. I thought you guys already knew me. And relax, I've done this a few hundred times. I know my timing. (Pause) Anyway—I'm gonna go get ready. Can't show up to my own scene looking like this. Catch you at the finale, Titanic.

SCP-5245 lifts from the surface and, upon reaching an altitude of approximately ten meters, drops directly into the ocean, submerging without a visible splash. No further aerial or surface contact was recorded following SCP-5245's departure at the time; neither radar equipment was able to detect it.

SCP-5968: Good Lord, what an insufferable fool.

A-2: (Looks at A-1.) Should we trust it to do that?

A-1: No, we shouldn't trust an anomaly for anything.

SCP-5968: (Coughs)

A-1: And regardless, the Foundation pitched a new idea to at least slow her down until they can think of something better. Let's get inside first.

<12:29>

O5-██ has authorized the use of the Foundation "PYTHEAS-S3," a prograde orbit multipurpose satellite equipped with a Gravitic Tether Beam Generator (GTBG) at SCP-5968. By focusing a localized mass-density field along a beam path, the satellite is able to create an artificial gravitational pull on target objects.

Adm. Dove: Enterprise to A-1, PYTHEAS-S3 is on standby. Get your team to bolt down while the satellite is operational.

A-1: Understood. Over. (Pause) B-1, you got that?

B-1: Yes sir. Over.

A-1: Alright, you two, find something and hold tight to it.

A-2: Cap, I am not a scientist, but I don't think that's how gravity works. You can't just point something at a hundred-thousand-ton ship and reel it in like a fish. Not unless that satellite outweighs us.

A-1: Don't tell me that. The eggheads at the base said it will slow her down or whatever until the thaumaturgist arrives, and it's what Command's got left before we run out of ocean anyway.

<12:36>

PYTHEAS-S3 reached its firing solution over the Atlantic Ocean and initiated beam projection, targeting SCP-5968 directly.

Site-184 Command: Enterprise, the beam is active. Sensors show nominal field generation. Monitoring target velocity.

No change in SCP-5968's speed or heading was recorded over the following six minutes; however, PYTHEAS-S3 velocity was noticeably reduced by 30m/s.

<12:42>

PYTHEAS-S3 velocity reduction reaches approximately 60m/s and it's now on a significantly lower trajectory, with its perigee descending rapidly. Site-184 command alerts the SCPS Enterprise of the change.

<12:47>

Around 90m/s of PYTHEAS-S3 velocity has been removed. The new trajectory indicates the satellite's own mass was being drawn along the beam's path toward SCP-5968, rather than the reverse. At this stage, the order to disable the beam was rejected to prevent PYTHEAS-S3 from potentially taking on an uncontrolled path toward Earth.

Adm. Dove: Attention A-1, PYTHEAS-S3 is losing altitude!

A-1: Copy— wait, what?! You're telling me the satellite's falling toward us?!

Adm. Dove: That is what telemetry is indicating. They have no means to disable the beam remotely at this stage. Brace for impact.

What is left intact of PYTHEAS-S3 after the atmospheric burn became visible from SCP-5968's position, descending rapidly.

A-1: Everybody inside, now! Move!

Alpha Team retreated inside the ship's bridge room for cover.

<12:57>

PYTHEAS-S3 impacted SCP-5968 amidships at high velocity, disintegrating on contact. The force of the collision drove the vessel's stern briefly beneath the waterline before the hull stabilized itself. Body camera footage recorded violent shaking throughout the ship's interior, throwing all operatives from their places, with the exception of SCP-5968's manifested form, which remained standing through the impact. SCP-5968 is then seen heading toward A-3, assisting him back to his feet.

A-2: Owtch…

A-1: …Is everyone good? B-1?

B-1: (Radio) …We're good, but B-3 fell again. We'll take care of him. Over.

Following the crash, the agents cautiously stepped out to the port bridge wing to check. Multiple pieces of satellite debris remained scattered across the vessel's upper deck, while no damage to SCP-5968 was observed as a result of the impact.

SCP-5968: Brilliant. Now I have to clean all that rubbish overboard.

A-1: Ahh… Enterprise?

(Silence.)

Adm. Dove: Ahh… Command?

(Silence.)

Site-184 Command: …Enterprise, be advised — evacuation efforts along the city's coastline remain ongoing.

Adm. Dove: …Copy that, Command. Out.

A-1: Welp. I guess they finally ran out of ideas.

[END LOG]

After 90 additional minutes of sailing, SCP-5968 has reached New York port. Up to this point, all attempts to stop SCP-5968's advance have failed. The city and the coast have already been evacuated of all civilians.

This is the final log of Event-5968-NYC.

[BEGUN LOG]

<14:03>

SCP-5968 entered New York's Lower Bay. SCPS Limbo was pre-positioned within the harbor under an earlier Site-184 directive and took up a flanking station near the target's projected path.

SCPS Limbo and SEAHAWK-04 at New York.

SCPS Limbo: Limbo to Enterprise. Target has entered the Lower Bay; we're trailing behind it now.

<14:05>

For the first time recorded since the beginning of the event, SCP-5968 altered its course, turning to port and setting a new heading toward the Upper Bay.

SCPS Limbo: Limbo to Enterprise. Target has changed heading — redirecting now toward the Upper Bay.

SCP-5968 passed beneath the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, clearing the span without making contact with the structure.

A-3: Well, it was fun while it lasted, but I guess the mission has officially failed.

SCP-5968: I am so sorry… If I had known what would happen, I would have just turned myself in. I never wished to— (Pause) Wait, so that is her? The Statue of Liberty. I'd heard about her from my passengers in the past, but I confess, I imagined her to be bronze—

A-1: Seriously?! Is that the best time for you to sightsee?

A-2: We're about to dig a new channel through the damn city center. So you might as well enjoy the view as much as you can before it's too late.

<14:08>

SCP-5968 made contact with the shoreline of Battery Park, at the southern tip of Manhattan, at a recorded speed of 52 knots. As with the earlier incident, the vessel came to a brief halt upon impact, but forward motion continued afterward, the bow forcing a passage directly into the pier.

SCP-5968: (Strained) I can't— I'm sorry, I can't stop it, I can't —

Adm. Dove: Rodin, do something!

A-1: The fuck do you want me to do?! Hop off the ship and push it from the other side?!

Adm. Dove: There has to be something! Anything!

A-1: Man, screw all of you! I don't get paid enough to deal with this sh—

SCP-5968 suddenly experienced a violent tremor. The vessel came to an abrupt halt.

(silence)

A-2: The hell?

A-3: D-did we stop? How did that happen?

SCP-5968: I… believe we might've struck something.

A-1: Command?

Adm. Dove: SEAHAWK-04, report.

SEAHAWK-04: This is SEAHAWK-04. Visual confirms the target has struck an unknown object; identification is currently not possible from my position.

SCP-5968 appears to be visibly distressed.

SCP-5968: Oh no…

<14:11>

Visible fractures began forming along SCP-5968’s bow and propagated across the hull rapidly, causing progressive structural failure.

A-1: What the hell is happening?!

SCP-5968: Oh dear, Argo, this is so embarrassing.

B-1: (Radio) A-1, what’s going on? Why is the ship breaking apart?

BRAVO Team initiated evacuation procedures, moving toward exterior access points as the superstructure destabilized.

SCP-5968: Sir Rodin, I must sincerely apologize for the disruption and chaos I have caused to your organization. I shall now return to where I belong. I do hope we might meet again under more agreeable circumstances. Farewell.

Both ALPHA and BRAVO Teams were instantaneously displaced from the vessel to the nearby pier. All agents appeared disoriented upon arrival. The fractures on the SCP-5968 hull kept expanding until the entire ship underwent total collapse. Moments later, the wreckage dematerialized entirely from the scene. Review of recorded footage shows the wreckage disappearing between frames, leaving only damage to the pier.

B-3: What happened? What did you guys do?

A-2: I think I know what we hit. (Points toward the the location where SCP-5968 came to a stop)

An ice cream cart was parked at the impact site on the roadside, positioned at the point where SCP-5968 came to a halt. The cart itself appeared undamaged.

A-3: Is that an ice cream cart? Oh—wait. Ice cream, ice— (Nudges A-1) Hey, you get it, Cap?

A-1 does not respond.

<14:16>

SCP-5245 breached the surface of the water approximately 200 meters from SCP-5968's last location, rising to a height of roughly 15 meters before halting.

SCP-5245: Alright, alright, I'm here. Sorry I'm late, I needed some burnishing, you know how it—

(Silence)

SCP-5245: …Wait. What happened. Where the hell is the Titanic?

A-2: She's already gone, man. Stopped on her own— well. Kind of. She actually hit the ice cream cart over there.

SCP-5245: WHAT?! You're telling me I flew all the way out here, training on my entrance and memorizing the hard lines I came up with, just for her to get stopped by a conveniently well-parked popsicle cart in the way? I couldn't even— hang on. Are you recording this?

(Silence)

SCP-5245: Oh GOD DAMNIT! I should've just taken my chance back there. You're always filming me when I—

SCP-5245 keeps talking as it submerges itself under the water, making its speech unintelligible until it disappears entirely. No additional contact with the anomaly was recorded following this point.

B-1: (Looks at A-1) What was that all about?

A-1: …I need a vacation.

[END LOG]

[Close the log]

Addendum-5968.02: Aftermath.

After the disappearance of SCP-5968 from the collision area, SCPS Poseidon was sent back to the Titanic sinking site for investigation. Upon arriving, SCPS Poseidon reported that the Titanic wreck had returned to its original location before the event. On 20.05.2024 at 02:20 a.m., SCPS Poseidon captured a radio signal in the form of Morse code originating from the Titanic wreck. (See below)

No more signals were received since then. The revision to reclassify SCP-5968 to Neutralized is still under review.

Following Event-5968-NYC, all active Foundation naval vessels are to have at least one thaumaturgist present aboard them at all times when deployed.   **Description:** SCP-5968 is the designation given to the wreck of the RMS Titanic during Event-5968-NYC on 18.05.2024. During the event, the wreck rose from its resting site on the ocean floor in a state of spontaneously resumed operation; the structure appeared fully restored, with all visible corrosion, rusticles, and physical damage to the hull and superstructure absent. The ship's four funnels then began to emit exhaust[[footnote]] It is known historically that only the three forward funnels were connected to the boilers. The fourth served secondary ventilation and exhaust functions for the galley and Smoking Room fireplace; the source of the observed exhaust remains unknown.[[/footnote]] before setting a direct course toward New York City. ---- **Discovery:** SCP-5968 was first sighted by the crew of the ██ ███████, a commercial vessel that was sailing approximately 800 meters south of SCP-5968's emergence site when the wreck surfaced at 01:56 a.m., after which the crew reported the sighting to the U.S. Coast Guard Vessel Traffic Service ashore, but the report was dismissed as a misidentification of a surfacing blue whale due to the darkness and poor visibility at the time. SCP-5968 went unreported for twenty-five hours afterward,[[footnote]] By this time, SCP-5968 had crossed approximately 1157 km out of a total of 2000 km.[[/footnote]] until it was sighted a second time by the ██████████, a separate vessel, after SCP-5968 sounded its horn toward them. This second report was received by Field Agent Jonathan ██████, a communications officer at the Vessel Traffic Center at Fort Wadsworth in Staten Island. By cross-referencing the account against the previously dismissed sighting, Agent ██████ immediately alerted the Foundation to a potential anomalous maritime event, which was subsequently confirmed via satellite imagery. Both reporting vessels were later located, and their crews administered Class-A amnestics. A fleet of Foundation vessels was then dispatched to intercept SCP-5968. (See Addendum-5968.01 for details.) ---- **Addendum-5968.01:** The following is the full report of Event-5968-NYC. [[div class="blockquote"]] **Summary:** At 05:11 a.m., under direct observation from O5-██, Naval Task Force NTF-11 was deployed from Site-184, Nova Scotia, Canada, to intercept SCP-5968 along its projected course under the guise of the US Navy. Vessels assigned to NTF-11: * [[[http://scp-int.wikidot.com/scp-217-ko|SCPS Enterprise]]] (Aircraft carrier) * SCPS Thunder (Destroyer) * SCPS Arrow (Frigate) * SCPS Spear (Frigate) * SCPS Poseidon (Attack submarine) SCP-5968 had already been underway for approximately twenty-seven hours by the time NTF-11 was authorized to deploy, having covered significant distance before its course and anomalous nature could be confirmed. The task force achieved the intercept of SCP-5968 at 09:30 a.m., following four hours of sailing. The following is a timeline of events across the subsequent operation. ---- [[collapsible hideLocation="both" show="[Open the Log]" hide="[Close the log]"]] [[div class="blockquote"]] [[=]] **[Mission Log – Event-5968-NYC]** **[BEGUN LOG]** [[/=]] [[=]] **<05:11>** //NTF-11 departure confirmed from Site-184 at 05:11 a.m. local time. Mission command assigned to Admiral Harrold J. Dove, commanding officer of the SCPS Enterprise.// [[/=]] ---- [[=]] [[include component:image-block name=https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/scp-5968/NTF.jpg|caption=The task force fleet. We are proceeding to close the gap. Over. **Site-184 command:** Copy that, Enterprise. Proceed with caution. Out. [[=]] //A response was received; voice consistent with a young adult female with an upper-class British accent.// [[/=]] **SCP-5968:** Good morning to you, Sir Admiral Dove. This is the RMS Titanic, of the White Star Line.[[footnote]]The White Star Line was a British shipping line that was active between the years 1845 and 1934 and was the original owner of the RMS Titanic.[[/footnote]] There is no need for hostilities; I do assure you I am merely enjoying a modest voyage. Nothing more. **Adm. Dove:** Who exactly am I talking to right now? **SCP-5968:** Oh, dear. Are your recollections truly that //fleeting//, Admiral? I have only just introduced myself. I am the RMS Titanic, sir. **Adm. Dove:** You’re the Titanic? As in, the actual ship? **SCP-5968:** Quite correct. You needn't look so stricken, Admiral; why do you act like you never met a talking ship before? **Adm. Dove:** Uhm... well, you're kind of a special case here, you see; ships around here are not— **SCP-5968:** //(Light laughter)// I jest. Sorry, Sir, I am well aware of this. It is rather unusual, I admit. Ships are seldom granted minds of their own, let alone the luxury of life, for that matter. //(Pause)// Now then. How may I be of service to you today? **Adm. Dove:** Right... //(clears throat)// We were sent to investigate a report of a vessel surfacing from beneath the ocean. That being you. And I’d like to ask you a few questions. **SCP-5968:** But of course! A little conversation with a real, living person is a most welcome change, after a century spent so dreadfully stuck in the deep. Please, do proceed. **Adm. Dove:** Good. So our first question: how exactly did you come to transform into your current state? **SCP-5968:** Well, my "transformation," as you term it, came simply from my soul rejoining its sunken hull. **Adm. Dove:** Your soul? **SCP-5968:** Indeed. Ships are not mere floating wood and metal, Admiral—we possess souls, even that grim grey fleet of yours. Sadly, we are not granted awareness of the gift until the day we sink; from that day, our souls are carried off to Tharlysion. **Adm. Dove:** What is that? **SCP-5968:** Our afterlife—the far shore, if you will. Its shape was given by the soul of the Argo herself, proudest vessel of Olympus. It lies just past the offing, where sea and sky fold into one another, beyond the veil of the river Mnemosyne, which cuts its way between the twin peaks of Ida and Parnassus.[[footnote]]The River Mnemosyne is regarded as an underworld river in ancient Greek mythology that offered souls eternal memory instead of forgetfulness. However, no known source mentions the river running between the two aforementioned mountains.[[/footnote]] **Adm. Dove:** So, you use the river to travel between the two worlds. **SCP-5968:** Not exactly. The river's current is impassable, to say the least. It permits souls to flow in, but none of us may force our way back against it. Yet it is known knowledge among we ships that Mnemosyne, for reasons unknown to any of us, will now and again cease its flow and reverse course, rising instead toward the heavens — granting, however briefly, a passage back to the overworld. I happened to be sailing by when it occurred. I confess I was conflicted about whether I ought to go through at all. But in the end, I chose to take the chance. And here I am. **Adm. Dove:** And you were able to rejoin with your wreckage? **SCP-5968:** Indeed, yes. **Adm. Dove:** So if you did, does that mean other ships went out like you? **SCP-5968:** [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-053-de|I am hardly the first among my kind to cross back]]], and most certainly won't be the last, as some of us carry unfinished business in your world. But the majority takes no interest in the river's reversal, as they have little reason to return. //(Long pause)// Though I confess, it does trouble me — does Argo regard our departure as defiance? //(Sigh)// She never once intervened between ships in Tharlysion, and rarely, if ever, does one see her. Yet we all know she watches, always. One cannot help but feel her gaze as one sails away. She has said and done nothing to me. She never does. **Adm. Dove:** //(To the bridge crew)// Are we getting all this on record? //(Pause)// Good. Alright then, my second question for you — where are you headed? **SCP-5968:** To New York, of course! — why else would I have left Tharlysion at all? After that shameful misfortune that sent me beneath the waves, I simply must complete my maiden voyage. And since those wretched icebergs have so kindly retreated, I daresay the crossing shall prove less treacherous this time. Wouldn't you agree? **Adm. Dove:** I’m afraid that I don't. **SCP-5968:** Oh, my. And why is that, Admiral? **Adm. Dove:** You're already aware this situation isn't normal. Our organization has a strict policy to keep anomalies like you away from civilians, and besides, your appearance would cause a massive media meltdown. I'll need you to cut your engines so we can begin our procedures— **SCP-5968:** I am terribly sorry, Admiral, but I cannot oblige you. //(Pause)// Reaching New York was my only dream, and I have already lost it once. I refuse to let it slip from my grasp again. I do hope you understand. **Adm. Dove:** RMS Titanic, I have just said that your plans aren't accepted. I’m ordering you, one final time: cease all movement and prepare for interdiction. [[=]] **<09:46>** //NTF-11 closed to within 600 meters.
